In accordance with the approved audit plan, the independent office of the city auditor has completed the continuous assurance audit.
Conscious assurance is an approach used to assess the effectiveness of business process controls on an ongoing basis.
Three analysis and the use of technology.
This includes analyzing large volumes of data to provide assurance on the whole population and closer to the occurrence of transactions.
The objective of the audit was to assess the effectiveness of controls related to key business areas, which included payroll, procurement and payments,
B cards and access to systems.
This is the first time the office has undertaken a continuous assurance audit.
The implementation of fusion has greatly helped in making the data available for analysis.
There were a few control tests which were not conducted.
You do lack of availability of data at this time.
However, as a fusion system ensures, we understand that more data and reporting will be available in the future to help us conduct more data analytics.
Based on the criteria used to assess controls, we did not find any evidence of occurrence of fraud or material inaccurate payments.
However, we noted that there is a need to improve processes and controls around employee time sheet submission and approval, employees vacation balances, procurement process,
Segregation of incompatible duties, management of P cards, and departed contractors and employees access to the system.
Summary of key recommendations arising from the audit include,
Stranding processes to ensure that employee time sheets are timely submitted and approved,
and Stranding management and monitoring of vacation balances.
Undertic measures to avoid segregation of duties issues, Stranding processes to ensure that purchasing protocols are followed,
and obtain vendor physical addresses where possible.
Stranding controls over management of P cards, and Stranding controls related to managing network accounts for departed contractors and employees.
Due to fraud related risks and cybersecurity risks, detailed findings and recommendations related to segregation of duties,
and access to systems will be presented in camera.
The administration has agreed with all the recommendations and has provided administrative responses and action plans to implement the recommendations.
The independent office of the city auditor will obtain regular status updates from administration on the implementation of the recommendations,
and will conduct follow-ups to assess whether these recommendations are effectively implemented.
A follow-up report will be provided to the committee in 2024.
